issues.t: Manual shifter cable clip can break (recall)
issues.sym: On a 5-speed manual, the shifter suddenly feels disconnected and you can no longer change gears.
issues.why: On certain manual-transmission Aerios the clip holding the shift cable to the shift lever was the wrong shape. Pushing the lever hard sideways into first gear can make the clip hit the housing, and over time it can snap and let the cable fall off.
issues.next: If the shifter goes limp, pull over safely and have the car towed. Ask a Suzuki dealer or call Suzuki with your VIN to see whether the recall clip replacement was done.

issues.t: Windshield may not be bonded securely (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see. In a crash the windshield could come loose.
issues.why: On some early cars the paint under the windshield adhesive did not stick well to the layer below it, so the glass may not be held in place as firmly as it should be.
issues.next: Check the recall status with your VIN. Wear seat belts every trip, since the windshield helps keep occupants inside in a crash.

issues.t: Rear tires wear out early from alignment
issues.sym: The rear tires wear unevenly or go bald on the edges long before the fronts, sometimes in only a few thousand miles.
issues.why: The factory rear alignment settings left the wheels angled in a way that scrubs the tires. Suzuki issued updated alignment specifications for shops to use.
issues.next: Have a four-wheel alignment done and ask the shop to use Suzuki's revised rear alignment specs. Check tire wear again a few thousand miles later.

issues.t: Front brake pads wear out quickly
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding from the front wheels, or the shop says the front pads are worn out after a short time.
issues.why: Owners report the front pads wearing much faster than expected, and Suzuki issued a service bulletin about the front pads on these cars.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected at the first squeal. Replacing pads before they wear to the metal saves the rotors. Grinding means stop driving and get them checked right away.

issues.t: Overheating at idle or radiator failure
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs while stopped or in traffic, the A/C may shut off, or you see coolant leaking from the front of the car.
issues.why: Owners report overheating at higher mileage. Causes found include a failing radiator, thermostat or hoses, and problems with the cooling fan.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs toward hot, pull over and shut the engine off. Do not open the hot radiator cap. Have the cooling system and fan pressure-tested before driving further.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the coolant level keeps dropping.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears out over time and starts to leak coolant.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and have the leak traced. A leaking pump can quickly lead to overheating.

issues.t: Heater core leak, costly to replace
issues.sym: Weak heat, a sweet coolant smell inside, foggy windows, or damp carpet on the passenger side.
issues.why: The heater core behind the dashboard can leak. On the Aerio much of the dash and center console must come apart to replace it, so labor is high.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested. Get more than one quote, since labor varies a lot for this job.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure and flashing check engine light
issues.sym: The engine shakes or misfires and the check engine light flashes, sometimes with no warning.
issues.why: One of the ignition coils that fires the spark plugs can fail, causing a misfire.
issues.next: A flashing check engine light means a misfire that can damage the catalytic converter. Drive gently and have the codes read soon.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: Battery or charging light on, dim lights, or the car dies and will not restart.
issues.why: Suzuki issued a service bulletin on alternator replacement for these years. A worn alternator stops charging the battery.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. If the battery light comes on while driving, head for a shop before the car runs out of power.

issues.t: Rusted exhaust pipes and catalytic converter
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, rattles under the car, or a check engine light for the catalytic converter.
issues.why: Owners report rusted exhaust clamps, pipes and converters, especially in road-salt areas.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected. Leaks before the muffler can let fumes into the cabin, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Rust on suspension and underbody parts
issues.sym: Visible rust underneath, or clunks and play in the suspension on older cars from road-salt areas.
issues.why: Suzuki sent dealers a reminder to check suspension and related parts on these cars for rust from road salt and other road chemicals.
issues.next: Have a shop look underneath during each oil change, especially before buying a used Aerio from a snowy state.

issues.t: Manual transmission pops out of 5th gear
issues.sym: On a manual car, the shifter jumps out of 5th gear while cruising.
issues.why: Suzuki issued a bulletin with a parts list for repairing worn 5th gear synchronizers and related gear parts inside the manual transaxle.
issues.next: Avoid holding the shifter in gear by hand. Have a shop confirm the cause; the repair means opening the transmission.

issues.t: Popping noise on slight turns
issues.sym: A pop or click from the front when turning the wheel gently, such as on curves or in parking lots.
issues.why: Suzuki issued a service bulletin for this noise, so it was a known issue on early Aerios. Front strut mounts and suspension joints are the usual places a shop checks.
issues.next: Have the front suspension and steering inspected, and mention the Suzuki bulletin for popping on slight turns.

issues.t: Side mirror works loose
issues.sym: The driver or passenger outside mirror wobbles, vibrates or will not hold its position.
issues.why: Suzuki issued a bulletin for loose side mirrors on Aerio sedans and wagons.
issues.next: Have the mirror mount tightened or repaired so it does not shake or fall off.

issues.t: Seat belts retract slowly or not fully
issues.sym: The seat belt hangs loose or is slow to wind back in after you unbuckle.
issues.why: Suzuki issued a service bulletin for slow or incomplete seat belt retraction.
issues.next: A belt that does not retract can still be worn, but have it checked so it locks and fits properly.

issues.t: Rattling exhaust heat shield
issues.sym: A tinny rattle from under the car, often at certain engine speeds or over bumps.
issues.why: The brackets holding the exhaust heat shield rust and break, so the shield vibrates.
issues.next: A shop can re-secure or remove the loose shield. It is a cheap fix.

issues.t: Broken exhaust hangers
issues.sym: The exhaust or muffler hangs low, bangs on bumps, or drones.
issues.why: The rubber hangers and clips that hold up the exhaust wear out and break.
issues.next: Have the hangers replaced before the pipe breaks or drags.

issues.t: Cracked or worn serpentine belt
issues.sym: Squealing from the engine, especially at startup, or visible cracks on the belt.
issues.why: The accessory drive belt dries out and starts to come apart with age and mileage.
issues.next: Replace the belt before it breaks; if it snaps you lose charging and the water pump can stop.

issues.t: Oxygen sensor failure
issues.sym: Check engine light on, sometimes with lower fuel economy.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors in the exhaust wear out at high mileage and send bad readings.
issues.next: Have the codes read to confirm which sensor is at fault before replacing it.

issues.t: Front strut or axle failure
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension, the car pulling, or in rare cases a broken axle while driving.
issues.why: Owners filed several complaints about the front suspension and MacPherson struts, and one reported a front axle breaking at high mileage.
issues.next: Any new clunk or sudden pulling should be checked soon. If the car makes a loud bang and will not move, stop and have it towed.

issues.t: Keyless entry remote stops working
issues.sym: The key fob no longer locks or unlocks the doors.
issues.why: Owners report the keyless entry quitting; the fob, its battery or the receiver can be at fault.
issues.next: Try a new fob battery first. If that does not work, a shop can test the receiver and reprogram a fob.
